title: Canonical pullback and scalar change of whole quotient systems
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and an embedding $\iota:E\to L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For the small pro-etale site of every scheme $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], use the ringed sequence site with its actual positive quotient rings and quotient-linear transitions [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Define the direct image of quotient systems by sectionwise base change and the canonical constant coefficient ring map. Define inverse image as its left adjoint and its exact derived functor. Define scalar change by the universal cochain-normalized derived change of rings for the map of quotient coefficient sheaves [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Define the composition comparison by the mate of the fibre-product-pasting map on direct images [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], the identity comparison by the inverse-image unit formula, and the scalar/pullback and scalar-composition comparisons by their tensor-generator formulas on the entire quotient diagram, before taking a limit. More explicitly, write $\gamma_f(x)$ for the ordinary inverse-image adjunction unit on a section at $(n,U)$. The scalar/pullback map sends $1\otimes\gamma_f(x)$ to $\gamma_f(1\otimes x)$. For $E\xrightarrow{\iota}L\xrightarrow{j}M$ the scalar associator sends $c\otimes(b\otimes x)$ to $c\,j(b)\otimes x$, and identity scalar change sends $s\otimes x$ to $sx$. The composition map is the inverse-image mate of the direct-image map induced by canonical fibre-product pasting. These formulas are natural in vertical site restrictions and horizontal quotient maps; derived comparisons are their localizations on K-flat complexes, using the universal cochain change-of-rings counits.

proof.text: For integralComparisonSequenceBaseChange_continuous, the structured-arrow category of the product base-change functor is equivalent to the product of the two structured-arrow categories. The identity and pro-etale base change are representably flat, so the product is representably flat. A covering of the sequence site is detected by its vertical slice. Pro-etale base change preserves that covering, and its image is contained in the vertical slice of the pushed-forward sieve. Cover preservation and representable flatness imply continuity. This step is proved in Lean.

For integralComparisonSequenceRing_naturality, first compose the constant-section coefficient map with the sheafification unit. The sheafification adjunction identifies the composite with the constant section on the base-changed object. Apply the adjunction injectively and use naturality of the two sheafification units to prove naturality in the coefficient ring. NatTrans.ofOpSequence then assembles the quotient-level maps. Uncurrying and precomposition with the product-opposite equivalence give naturality on the whole sequence site. This step is proved in Lean.

For integralComparisonSequenceScalar_naturality, apply functorial constant sheafification to integralScalarQuotientMap_transition from [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined]. NatTrans.ofOpSequence assembles the scalar inclusions into a natural transformation of coefficient sequences. Uncurrying and the product-opposite equivalence give the required equality for every sequence-site arrow. This step is proved in Lean.

For integralComparisonSequenceDirectImage_isRightAdjoint, [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] gives the Grothendieck abelian structure on the source module-sheaf category in max(u,t+1). Mathlib supplies a coseparator and well-poweredness. To prove limit preservation, forget to module presheaves and evaluate on each sequence-site object. The resulting cone is obtained by evaluating the original cone on the base-changed object and restricting scalars, both limit-preserving operations. Evaluations jointly reflect limits, and the sheaf forgetful functor reflects limits. Apply Mathlib isRightAdjoint_of_preservesLimits_of_isCoseparating. This step is proved in Lean and replaces the direct Kan-extension construction for adjoint existence.

The seven remaining named obligations retain their original docstring arguments: prove exactness by the constant-coefficient inverse image and levelwise exactness; construct composition and unit maps by fibre-product pasting and adjunction mates; construct scalar associators and unit maps on balanced tensor generators and sheafify; localize the scalar/pullback associator on K-flat complexes using the universal cochain scalar counits. These obligations remain sorry in this partial delivery, not asserted proved.
